slides.title: The `` Tag 🏞️
slides.content: # A Void Element That Embeds Visuals `` is a void (self‑closing) element that displays an image file. Two essential attributes: - `src` – path to the image file. - `alt` – alternative text description. ```html ``` The `alt` text is crucial for accessibility and appears if the image fails to load.

slides.title: Why `alt` Matters ♿
slides.content:
# Accessibility and SEO

Screen readers read the `alt` text aloud. Search engines use it to understand image content.

- Always include an `alt` attribute. If the image is purely decorative, use `alt=""` (empty string) to hide it from screen readers.
- Describe the image's **content or function**, not just "picture".
- Don't use `alt` for SEO keyword stuffing – it harms accessibility.

Good: `alt="Profile photo of Jane Doe"`
Bad: `alt="woman headshot business professional corporate"`

quizData.question: It's okay to leave out the `alt` attribute if the image is just decorative.
quizData.explanation: You should include `alt=""` (empty) for decorative images. Omitting the attribute completely is invalid HTML and can cause screen readers to read the filename.

slides.title: Controlling Image Size 📏
slides.content: # Width and Height Attributes You can specify `width` and `height` on the `` tag (values in pixels, no unit). ```html ``` This helps the browser reserve space before the image loads, preventing layout shifts. Modern best practice: use CSS for responsive sizing, but HTML dimensions act as a fallback.
